properties.title: Cosmos-Surg-dVRK: World Foundation Model-based Automated Online Evaluation of Surgical Robot Policy Learning
properties.contribution_type: Primary method – new simulator + evaluation pipeline

membership.reason: Cosmos-Surg-dVRK is an action-conditioned surgical video World Foundation Model executing closed-loop online rollouts with surgical VLA policies and benchmarking sim-to-real success.
membership.counting_boundary: Verified L2 action-conditioned surgical video world model used as an online simulator for external VLA policy evaluation (WT_PROCEDURE, BP_FORECAST).

properties.backbone: Finetuned Cosmos-Predict2 action-conditioned World Foundation Model + V-JEPA 2 video success classifier

properties.flow: Initial surgical frame s_0 -> VLA policy (pi_0/GR00T) -> kinematic action -> Cosmos-Surg-dVRK autoregressive rollout s_{1:K} -> V-JEPA 2 success classifier

properties.purpose: Automated online simulation and benchmarking of autonomous surgical robot policies.
properties.environment: Tabletop suture-pad phantom + ex-vivo porcine cholecystectomy vs real dVRK Si

assertions.rationale: Finetunes Cosmos-Predict2 WFM and V-JEPA 2 video backbone.
Autoregressive video frame/latent state updated at each policy step.
Continuous robotic kinematic actions (Delta pos, Delta rot, jaw).

Action-conditioned future surgical frame prediction conditioned on 10 Hz kinematic action chunks (K=12) is evaluated quantitatively via holdout identical-trajectory L1/SSIM curves (Fig. 2, p. 3) and closed-loop online policy rollouts against real dVRK Si (Pearson r = 0.718 manual, r = 0.756 automated, p < 0.001; Avg MMRV = 0.10 +/- 0.04; ex-vivo 8/9 vs 7/9), with positive success bias (MBE 0.140-0.153) and physical hallucinations (Sec 5.2.3).

Future-state rollout predictions (K=12 frames per step, autoregressive over 500-1000 steps) are evaluated quantitatively via holdout frame-level L1 distance and SSIM vs. number of generated frames (Fig. 2, p. 3) and simulated-vs-real task success rates (Pearson r = 0.756, p < 0.001, MBE = 0.153; Tables 1-3, pp. 8-12), with observed positive bias and hallucinations.
Closed-loop policy-in-the-loop rollouts evaluating and selecting surgical policies (pi_0, GR00T).
Safe, reproducible online evaluation of surgical robot policies.
Action-conditioned soft-tissue rollout vs identical kinematic trajectory on real dVRK Si (L1/SSIM).
Automated policy success-rate benchmarking across Handover, Throw, Knot Tie, Pickup.
Sim-to-real correlation Pearson r = 0.756 (p < 0.001), mean bias 0.153, MMRV 0.10 against real dVRK Si.

evidence_fragments.content: We propose a framework for automated policy evaluation using Cosmos-Surg-dVRK, a Cosmos world foundation model (WFM) finetune, to perform simulated surgical policy rollouts and subsequent automated success rate evaluation using a video classifier. Evaluation proceeds by initializing the policy with an observed frame at state s 0. Conditioned on s 0, the policy and Cosmos-Surg-dVRK then generate K action-conditioned future frames autoregressively, s 1:K. In each iteration, the predicted frames are appended to the output video, and the last predicted frame is used as input to the surgical policy for the next iteration.

Figure 2: Soft tissue simulation with Cosmos-Surg-dVRK. Surgical simulation in ex-vivo porcine cholecystectomy. Top row: example as recorded on the real dVRK Si. Middle row: Cosmos-Surg-
dVRK generated example with identical kinematic action trajectory. Bottom row: Holdout L1 and SSIM vs. number of generated frames.

Finetuning the Cosmos-Predict2 variant that conditions on kinematic actions achieves two key benefits: (1) Training Cosmos WFM to predict future frames from the current state and predicted actions enables implicit modeling of the robot’s kinematic chain, removing the need for explicit articulation or kinematics specification; (2) Post-training an existing Cosmos WFM leverages broad pretraining for physics understanding, while additional finetuning on surgical data allows the model to learn domain-specific tissue and robot interactions.

and inference, at each iteration i, Cosmos WFM takes the current state s i and the policy-originated action sequence a i:i+K−1 = (ai, . . . , ai+K−1 ) with K = 12, and predicts the subsequent K frames ˆsi+1:i+K. For the next iteration i ′ = i + K, we set s i′ := ˆsi+K, so the model rolls forward autoregressively.

Most important for automated policy evaluation, we observe strong alignment with real-world policy ordering, with low disorder (Avg. MMRV = 0.10 ± 0.04). Moreover, a Pearson correlation of r = 0.756 (p < 0.001) indicates a strong, positive linear relationship between the Cosmos-Surg-dVRK with automated classifier success rates and the real-world dVRK Si success rates. Although the MBE rises to 0.153 versus 0.140 in human evaluations (see Table 2), further underscoring the inherent success bias observed earlier in the Cosmos-Surg-dVRK model, the overall statistical results closely match those of the human labeling experiment.

capability_assessments.rationale: Downgraded from L4 to L2: Cosmos-Surg-dVRK implements core persistent autoregressive state (s_i -> s_{i+K}), temporal transitions, and learned Cosmos-Predict2 dynamics, and quantitatively evaluates action-conditioned future rollouts via holdout L1/SSIM (Fig. 2) and simulated-vs-real dVRK policy benchmarking (Pearson r = 0.756, MMRV = 0.10, MBE = 0.153). However, the external VLA policies (pi_0, GR00T N1/N1.5, SRT-H) are trained on real demonstrations rather than optimized or planned inside the world model (planning.search_policy is absent/not implemented; matches legacy_cells.Z = 'L2 Action-conditioned prediction' and CH = 'None'). Additionally, policies are initialized from their respective dVRK rollouts rather than matched alternative actions from identical initial states (so L3 is not quantitatively established).

readiness_assessments.legacy_highest_label: R1 Phantom + ex-vivo sim-to-real dVRK validation

limitations: Evaluated on tabletop suture-pad phantoms and ex-vivo porcine tissue; no live human clinical surgery.

External VLA policies are evaluated in closed-loop simulation rather than optimized/planned inside the world model (L2, not L4); simulated rollouts exhibit positive success bias (MBE 0.140-0.153) and physical hallucinations.

legacy_cells.B: Cosmos-Surg-dVRK: World Foundation Model-based Automated Online Evaluation of Surgical Robot Policy Learning
legacy_cells.C: Zbinden, Lukas, Nelson, Nigel, Chen, Juo-Tung, Chen, Xinhao, Kim, Ji Woong, Azizian, Mahdi, et al.
legacy_cells.J: Primary method – application/adaptation of existing WM
legacy_cells.S: Can policy success rates from action-conditioned surgical video-model rollouts predict and rank the same policies’ outcomes on the dVRK Si robot?
legacy_cells.V: Select the most promising surgical robot policies for real-robot evaluation and deployment using simulated rollout success rates.
legacy_cells.AI: Endoscopic video frames; kinematic action sequences (relative translation, rotation, and jaw angle)
legacy_cells.AK: Cosmos-Predict2-2B-Video2World, an action-conditional pretrained Cosmos WFM variant, was fine-tuned.
legacy_cells.BD: Relative translation; rotation; absolute jaw angle; 10 Hz action sampling; K=12 actions per prediction chunk.
legacy_cells.BL: Video and kinematic action data sampled at 10 Hz; K=12 predicted frames/actions per iteration.
legacy_cells.BS: Autoregressively generated future surgical video frames, concatenated into policy rollout videos.
legacy_cells.BT: A separate V-JEPA 2 attentive-probe video classifier labels rollout events as success, anomaly, or default and maps rollout outcomes to success/failure.
legacy_cells.BV: For the V-JEPA 2 attentive-probe classifier, cross-entropy loss with loss scaling for false-positive and false-negative anomaly events.
legacy_cells.CD: Per-rollout step limits: 1,000 for needle throw; 750 for pickup, handover, and knot tying; 500 for cholecystectomy. The model predicts K=12 frames per iteration.
legacy_cells.DN: Tabletop suture pad dataset; porcine cholecystectomy dataset
legacy_cells.DQ: Tabletop suture pad: 3,036 episodes (~13 hours); porcine cholecystectomy: 16,506 episodes (~18 hours).
legacy_cells.EC: Policy-evaluation outcomes: simulated success rates and policy ranking were compared with real dVRK Si outcomes; manual rollout evaluation had Pearson r=0.718 (p<0.001), MBE=0.140, average MMRV=0.13±0.08; automated evaluation had r=0.756 (p<0.001), MBE=0.153, average MMRV=0.10±0.04.
legacy_cells.ED: Tabletop simulation-to-real policy evaluation: manual Pearson r=0.718 (p<0.001), MBE=0.140; automated Pearson r=0.756 (p<0.001), MBE=0.153. Ex-vivo cholecystectomy: dVRK 7/9 successes versus Cosmos-Surg-dVRK 8/9.
legacy_cells.EE: Two human raters labeled simulated tabletop rollouts; their agreement was ICC(2,1)=0.811. The V-JEPA 2 classifier versus human labels achieved ICC(2,1)=0.836 and Pearson r=0.840 (p<0.001).
legacy_cells.EK: Ablation compared Cosmos-Surg-dVRK fine-tuned on successes only versus successes plus failures. Manual MBE was 0.325 without failure episodes versus 0.140 for the full model; average MMRV was 0.146 versus 0.129.
legacy_cells.EL: Reported hallucinations include false positives (e.g., a needle snapping into a misaligned gripper) and false negatives (a needle falling despite a perfect grasp); the model is biased toward false positives. In cholecystectomy rollouts, failures included scissors missing the duct or grabbing/cutting the wrong tube.
legacy_cells.FL: An endoscopic video frame initializes Cosmos-Surg-dVRK; the fine-tuned Cosmos-Predict2 action-conditioned video model predicts K future frames from kinematic action chunks and rolls autoregressively. A surgical policy receives the latest generated frame and supplies the next action chunk; completed rollout video is scored by a separate V-JEPA 2 attentive-probe classifier.
legacy_cells.FM: Introduces an action-conditioned surgical fine-tune of Cosmos WFM for online evaluation of surgical robot policies; demonstrates task-specific agreement with real dVRK outcomes, automated classifier agreement with human labels, ex-vivo cholecystectomy evaluation, and an ablation showing the value of failure episodes.
legacy_cells.FN: For tabletop tasks, manual simulated-versus-real policy evaluations had Pearson r=0.718 (p<0.001); automated evaluations had r=0.756 (p<0.001). Automated-versus-human rollout labels had r=0.840 (p<0.001), ICC=0.836. Cholecystectomy success was 7/9 on dVRK and 8/9 in simulation. The simulator showed positive success bias (automated MBE=0.153).
legacy_cells.FO: The study uses a single camera and visual state without proprioception; generated videos show uncertainty/ambiguity around small objects. The authors report insufficiently learned physics and kinematics due to limited training-data coverage, with a false-positive success bias.
legacy_cells.FQ: The authors state that no generalizable, low-cost solution exists for faithful surgical policy evaluation during development because of soft-body-dynamics challenges in current simulators.
legacy_cells.FR: Evidence is limited to task-specific tabletop and ex-vivo porcine robot-policy evaluations, not prospective patient benefit or clinical deployment. Simulated outcomes correlate with real outcomes but have positive success bias and observed physical hallucinations; action conditioning and policy ranking do not establish causal identification or general simulator fidelity.
